objectives.text: Provide clarity for all non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) and other entities with regulatory AML program requirements (collectively 'covered NBFIs') on the AML/CFT Priorities.

citations.quote:
is 
issuing this statement to provide clarity for all non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) and 
other entities with regulatory AML program requirements (collectively “covered NBFIs”)4 on 
these AML/CFT Priorities.

objectives.text: FinCEN recognizes the need for revised regulations and timely guidance to assist covered NBFIs in complying with the BSA, and is committed to developing and publishing timely guidance and corresponding examination procedures for examiners.

citations.quote:
FinCEN recognizes the need for revised regulations and timely guidance to assist covered NBFIs 
in complying with the BSA.  FinCEN is committed to working with the Agencies to develop and 
publish timely guidance and corresponding examination procedures for examiners.

obligations.actor: the Secretary of the Treasury (in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators, relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies)
obligations.action: establish and make public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy (AML/CFT Priorities)

citations.quote:
The Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (the “ AML Act”)1 requires the Secretary of the 
Treasury, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators, 2 relevant 
State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies, to establish and make 
public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy 
(AML/CFT Priorities).

obligations.actor: FinCEN (in consultation with the Federal functional regulators and relevant State financial regulators)
obligations.action: as appropriate, promulgate regulations regarding the AML/CFT Priorities
obligations.trigger: within 180 days of the establishment of the AML/CFT Priorities

citations.quote:
The 
AML Act requires that, within 180 days of the establishment of the AML/CFT Priorities, 
FinCEN (in consultation with the Federal functional regulators and relevant State financial 
regulators) shall, as appropriate, promulgate regulations regarding the AML/CFT Priorities.

obligations.action: incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities into their risk-based AML programs
obligations.trigger: the effective date of the final regulations
exceptions: not required until the effective date of the final regulations

citations.quote:
Covered NBFIs are not required to incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities into their risk-based 
AML programs until the effective date of the final regulations.

obligations.action: start considering how they will incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities into their risk-based AML programs, such as by assessing the potential risks associated with the products and services they offer, the customers they serve, and the geographic areas in which they operate
obligations.trigger: in preparation for any new requirements when those final rules are published

citations.quote:
covered NBFIs may wish to 
start considering how they will incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities into their risk-based AML 
programs, such as by assessing the potential risks associated with the products and services 
they offer, the customers they serve, and the geographic areas in which they operate.

obligations.action: have its review of the AML/CFT Priorities and the incorporation of those Priorities, as appropriate, into its risk-based AML program included as a measure on which it is supervised and examined

citations.quote:
the AML Act requires that the review by a covered NBFI of the AML/CFT Priorities 
and the incorporation of those Priorities, as appropriate, into its risk-based AML program, be 
included as a measure on which it is supervised and examined.

obligations.action: examine covered NBFIs for the incorporation of the AML/CFT Priorities into their risk-based AML programs
obligations.trigger: until the effective date of final regulations
exceptions: applies until the effective date of final regulations

citations.quote:
This statement confirms that 
FinCEN will not examine covered NBFIs for the incorporation of the AML/CFT Priorities into 
their risk-based AML programs until the effective date of final regulations noted above.

obligations.action: request that the staff of any of the Agencies, or a self-regulatory organization (SRO) authorized to examine a covered NBFI, examine any covered NBFIs for this requirement (or any related state requirement)
obligations.trigger: until the effective date of final regulations
exceptions: applies until the effective date of final regulations

citations.quote:
FinCEN will not request that the staff of any of the Agencies, or a self-regulatory organization 
(SRO) authorized to examine a covered NBFI, examine any covered NBFIs for this requirement 
(or any related state requirement) until the effective date of final regulations.

interactions.description: The statement cross-references the AML program requirements for covered NBFIs across the 31 CFR part-210 provisions for each covered sector (banks without a Federal functional regulator, casinos and card clubs, MSBs, brokers or dealers in securities, mutual funds, insurance companies, futures commission merchants and introducing brokers, dealers in precious metals/stones/jewels, credit card system operators, loan or finance companies, and housing GSEs).

citations.quote:
See 31 CFR §§ 1020.210(b) (banks without a Federal functional regulator); 1021.210 (casinos and card 
clubs); 1022.210 (money services businesses); 1023.210 (brokers or dealers in securities); 1024.210 (mutual 
funds); 1025.210 (insurance companies); 1026.210 (futures commission merchants and introducing brokers 
in commodities)

interactions.description: FinCEN's examination authority and reliance on examinations by Federal functional regulators and the IRS is grounded in various BSA/statutory provisions and regulations, and references the FinCEN Enforcement Statement dated 8/18/2020.

citations.quote:

addition, relies on examinations conducted by Federal functional regulators and the Internal Revenue Service. 
31 U.S.C. § 5318(a)(3) and (b) (2012); 31 CFR § 1010.810 (2019).  See also FinCEN Enforcement Statement,

interactions.description: Separately, the federal banking agencies, State bank and credit union regulators, and FinCEN issued a parallel statement to provide clarity for banks on the AML/CFT Priorities.

citations.quote:
State bank and credit union regulators, and FinCEN also issued a statement to provide clarity for 
banks5 on the AML/CFT Priorities.

notes: This is agency guidance (evidence role: agency_guidance), not itself a program-establishment rule. It restates AML Act obligations located in 31 U.S.C. § 5318(h)(4) and defers substantive incorporation/examination duties until the effective date of future final regulations; the actual program 'pillars' obligations reside in the cross-referenced 31 CFR part-210 rules and the amended BSA, which are boundary/coordination sources here. The document's own scope is directed at 'covered NBFIs' (non-bank FIs including MSBs and broker-dealers, plus the SRO examination layer), which is within the ratified scope for those sectors; banks are addressed by a separate parallel statement noted only. Ambiguity preserved: the statement uses 'may wish to' for OBL-04, extracted as modality 'may'; and OBL-03/OBL-05 are contingent on final regulations / conditioned by 'as appropriate' and extracted as conditional/must respectively per the text's own 'not required until' and 'requires that' phrasing.
